596	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
597	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list.
598	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests`
599	  — open a two-stage retention cleanup request for the version's masking-hit
600	  records. Body contains exactly `reason` and `before`:
601	  `{"reason": "legal hold expired", "before": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`.
602	  `reason` must be a string that is non-empty after trimming whitespace;
603	  `before` must be an ISO-8601 date-time carrying a timezone (offset or `Z`),
604	  and a record belongs to the target set only when its hit write time is
605	  strictly earlier than that instant. Creating a request only returns a
606	  preview — no hit record is deleted or modified, and the record list,
607	  search, summary, diff, reconcile and trend responses stay unchanged.
608	  Returns `201` with `id`, `reason` (trimmed), `before` (echoed as
609	  submitted), `status` (`pending`), `created_at` and a `preview` block:
610	  `hit_count` (the number of records that would be cleaned up),
611	  `first_hit_at` / `last_hit_at` (the earliest and latest hit times in the
612	  target set, `null` when the set is empty) and `fields` (the distinct field
613	  names involved, sorted ascending; `[]` when empty). The target set is
614	  fixed at creation time: masking-hit records written afterwards never enter
615	  the request even when they precede the cutoff by clock time. At most one
616	  pending request may exist per version; creating another while one is open
617	  returns `409` and writes nothing (confirmed requests never block a new
618	  one). Unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing/non-string/blank `reason`,
619	  missing/unparseable/timezone-less `before`, an extra body field, a
620	  non-JSON/non-object body or any query parameter → `422` and nothing is
621	  written, with 404 taking precedence.
622	- `GET .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests` — list the
623	  version's cleanup requests sorted by request `id` ascending (empty when
624	  there are none). Confirmed requests stay listed and requests survive
625	  process restarts. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
626	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
627	- `POST .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests/{request_id}/confirm`
628	  — confirm a request with an empty request body and no query parameters.
629	  Confirmation atomically deletes exactly the target set frozen at creation
630	  and sets `status` to `confirmed`; the response is the request plus
631	  `confirmed_at` and `deleted_count` (the number of records actually
632	  deleted, possibly zero). Confirming an already-confirmed request returns
633	  `409` and never changes data again; concurrent confirmations have exactly
634	  one winner (the others get `409`) and can never leave the records half
635	  deleted. After a cleanup the surviving hit records keep their original
636	  `sequence` numbers and later hits continue the existing increasing run
637	  without reusing cleaned numbers; the record list and search return only
638	  surviving records, and summary, trend, diff and reconcile recompute from
639	  them. Access records are not cleaned up and the processing-task audit
640	  chain remains immutable. A request body or query parameter on the confirm
641	  endpoint → `422`; unknown dataset/version/request → `404` (precedence
642	  matches the hit-record reads), and confirming a confirmed request →
643	  `409`.
644	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-compliance-export` — read-only
645	  cross-version export of the dataset's whole privacy compliance state,
646	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or
647	  deleted, and no hit record, access record or cleanup request is touched).
648	  The path carries only the dataset name; the request takes no body and no
649	  query parameters (`422`); an unknown dataset → `404`, with the same
650	  404-before-422 precedence as the hit-record reads. A dataset without
651	  schema versions returns `200` with an empty `versions` array and all-zero
652	  totals, never an error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
653	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
654	
655	  ```json
656	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"policies":[...],"hit_count":0,"masked_count":1,"view_count":2,"cleanup_requests":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
657	  ```
658	
659	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
660	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
661	  has exactly `version`, `policies`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
662	  `view_count`, `cleanup_requests` in that order. `policies` lists the
663	  version's registered policies ordered by policy id; each policy has `id`,
664	  `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `allowed_roles` and `enabled`.
665	  `cleanup_requests` lists the version's cleanup requests ordered by request
666	  id (both pending and confirmed are retained); each has `id`, `reason`,
667	  `status` and `created_at`. `hit_count` is the number of masking-hit
668	  records currently stored for the version, `masked_count` is the sum of the
669	  access records' masked-value counts and `view_count` is the number of
670	  access records; all three reflect the records surviving a confirmed
671	  cleanup. `totals` has exactly `policy_count`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
672	  `view_count` and `cleanup_request_count`, each the sum of the per-version
673	  values over the whole dataset.
674	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-policy-coverage` — read-only cross-version
675	  check of the dataset's privacy policy coverage, computed fresh on every
676	  read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or deleted, and no policy
677	  or identification record is touched). The path carries only the dataset
678	  name; the request takes no body and no query parameters (`422`); an
679	  unknown dataset → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
680	  compliance export. A dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an
681	  empty `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
682	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly
683	  one trailing newline):
684	
685	  ```json
686	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"fields":[...],"candidates":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
687	  ```
688	
689	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
690	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
691	  has exactly `version`, `fields`, `candidates` in that order. `fields`
692	  lists every field of the version ordered by field name; each entry has
693	  `field`, `coverage`, `classification`, `masking` and `enabled`, where
694	  `coverage` is `enabled` (an enabled policy is registered), `disabled` (a
695	  policy is registered but disabled) or `unregistered` (no policy), and the
696	  last three keys report the registered policy's classification, masking and
697	  enabled state (all `null` when no policy is registered). `candidates`
698	  lists the advisory suggestions for fields that were identified with at
699	  least one name or sample hit but carry no privacy policy yet, ordered by
700	  identification record id ascending; each candidate has exactly `field`,
701	  `classification` and `masking`, and an identified field whose name and
702	  samples both missed does not appear. The candidates are a compliance
703	  self-check reference only: they never register a policy and never rewrite
704	  an identification record. `totals` has exactly `version_count`,
705	  `field_count`, `enabled_count`, `disabled_count`, `unregistered_count`
706	  and `candidate_count`, each the sum of the per-version values over the
707	  whole dataset.
708	
709	### Sensitive-field identification
710	
711	Sensitive-field identification produces candidate annotations for the fields of
712	a schema version. It complements the manual privacy policies but never creates
713	or modifies one: an identification is advisory only. Records (including their
714	stable ids) persist across restarts.
715	
716	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
717	  identify one field. The body contains exactly `field` and `samples`:
718	  `{"field": "contact_email", "samples": ["alice@example.com"]}`. `field` must
719	  name an existing field of the version; its name and type are taken from the
720	  version definition. `samples` is an array of JSON scalars (strings, numbers,
721	  booleans or `null`) and may be empty; objects or arrays reject the whole
722	  request. The samples are never stored or echoed back. Returns the record;
723	  the first submission for a field returns `201`, re-running the same field
724	  refreshes the record in place (the id is unchanged) and returns `200`.
725	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
726	  return every identification record of the version sorted by id ascending
727	  (empty when there are none). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
728	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
729	
730	  Each record has `id`, `field`, `field_type`, `evidence`, `confidence`,
731	  `source` and `created_at`. `source` references the identified field as
732	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. `evidence` is the ordered, de-duplicated
733	  list of hit kinds, name hits before sample hits:
734	
735	  - **Name hits** — the field name contains a sensitive word case-insensitively
736	    as a substring. The words are `email`, `phone`, `id_card`, `password`,
737	    `token` and `birth`, emitting `name:<word>` in that order.
738	  - **Sample hits** — only string sample values are inspected (numbers,
739	    booleans and `null` never hit), and only when the field's declared type is
740	    `string`; a field declared with any other type is matched by name alone,
741	    even when a sample looks like an email. `sample:email` requires exactly
742	    one `@` with non-empty text on both sides and a dot in the domain;
743	    `sample:phone` requires an 11-digit string starting with `1`. Either format
744	    matching is sufficient.
745	
746	  `confidence` is `high` when both the name and the samples hit, `medium` for
747	  samples only, `low` for the name only and `none` when neither side hits
748	  (`evidence` is then an empty list but the record is still generated).
749	
750	  One record is kept per field: a re-run overwrites the evidence and confidence
751	  in place with a stable id. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; a field that does
752	  not exist in the version → `404`; missing or extra body fields, a
753	  non-string or blank field name, a `samples` value that is not an array of
754	  scalars (objects and arrays included), an empty body, malformed JSON or any
755	  query parameter → `422` and nothing is written.
756	
757	#### Masking strategy suggestions
758	
759	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions`
760	  — read-only advisory masking-strategy candidates derived from the version's
761	  identification records. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
762	  parameters (`422` if either is present, with nothing written); unknown
763	  dataset/version → `404`. A version without identification records returns an
764	  empty list rather than an error.
765	
766	  Each candidate has exactly `field`, `classification`, `masking` and
767	  `allowed_roles`. Only records whose name or samples hit produce a candidate;
768	  a record with empty evidence is omitted. Candidates follow the identification
769	  records' `id` ascending and are recomputed on every read, so refreshing an
770	  identification changes the suggestion on the next request. The endpoint
771	  writes nothing, never registers a privacy policy and leaves the
772	  identification records' fields, ordering and refresh semantics untouched;
773	  the privacy view continues to mask according to registered policies only.
774	
775	  - `classification` is `PII` for email, phone, id-card and birthday hits, and
776	    `CREDENTIAL` for password and token hits. A field hitting both is `PII`.
777	  - `masking` reuses the privacy-view vocabulary: `partial` for `PII`
778	    candidates and `redact` for `CREDENTIAL` candidates (a both-kinds field
779	    takes `partial`); no new masking format is introduced.
780	  - `allowed_roles` is always an empty list: the suggested masking applies to
781	    every role, granting none an unmasked view.
782	
783	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions/register`
784	  — turn the current advisory candidates into registered privacy policies. The
785	  body contains only `{"fields": ["<field>", ...]}`: a non-empty array of
786	  distinct field names, each non-empty after trimming and naming an existing
787	  field of the version that currently has a masking suggestion candidate.
788	  Returns `201` with one privacy policy record per requested field, in the
789	  request's field-name order; each record has the same fields as the manual
790	  policy creation response (`id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`,
791	  `allowed_roles`, `enabled`, `created_at`), is enabled by default and gets a
792	  service-generated id and timestamp. Each policy copies its candidate's
793	  `classification` and `masking` verbatim with the candidate's empty
794	  `allowed_roles`, so after registration every role sees those fields masked;
795	  the next privacy view read masks according to the new policies. The whole
796	  batch is validated before anything is written, so any rejection writes no
797	  policy and no timestamp. Unknown dataset/version, or a named field that does
798	  not exist in the version → `404`; a field without an available candidate
799	  (never identified, or whose identification record currently yields no
800	  candidate) or one that already has a privacy policy → `409`; two concurrent
801	  registrations of the same field leave exactly one winner. Missing or extra
802	  body fields, an empty `fields` array, duplicate, non-string or blank names,
803	  an empty body, a whitespace-only body, malformed JSON or any query parameter
804	  → `422` and nothing is written. Registration only reads the identification
805	  records and field definitions; it never writes or auto-refreshes an
806	  identification, and the read-only suggestions endpoint stays unchanged.
807	
808	### Row snapshots
809	
810	A row snapshot persistently records the rows of a schema version at one point in
811	time. Snapshots (including their rows) survive restarts.
812	
813	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — persist a snapshot.
814	  Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}` where `rows` must be an array of JSON objects
815	  (it may be empty). The JSON values and the order of rows/object keys are deep
816	  copied verbatim. Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`,
817	  `created_at` and `row_count` (no rows). Unknown dataset/version → `404`;
818	  malformed or non-object rows → `422` and nothing is written.
819	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — list snapshot
820	  metadata sorted by `id` ascending (no `rows`).
821	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}` — return
822	  the metadata together with the saved `rows`. Unknown dataset/version/snapshot
823	  → `404`.
824	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at?timestamp=<ISO-8601>` —
825	  return the most recent snapshot whose `created_at` is not later than
826	  `timestamp`, including its rows. The timestamp must be a timezone-aware
827	  ISO-8601 date-time (an offset or trailing `Z`): missing, invalid or
828	  timezone-less values return `422`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; when no
829	  snapshot exists at or before the timestamp the response is `404`.
830	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at/diff?from=<ISO-8601>&to=<ISO-8601>`
831	  — read-only time-travel row diff, appended one segment after the bare-row
832	  time lookup and accepting GET only. Each of `from` (the baseline) and `to`
833	  (the target) must be a timezone-aware ISO-8601 date-time; each side
834	  independently selects the latest snapshot whose `created_at` is not later
835	  than its own timestamp (the same selection as the bare-row lookup), so the
836	  two times may resolve to the same snapshot and a `to` earlier than `from` is
837	  valid — the two snapshots are simply compared in their named order. The
838	  comparison reads snapshots and rows and writes nothing. The JSON document
839	  is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
840	  newline) with top-level keys `from_timestamp`, `to_timestamp`,
841	  `from_snapshot_id`, `to_snapshot_id`, `added`, `removed`, `fields_added`
842	  and `fields_removed` in that order; the timestamps echo the submitted query
843	  values. `added` and `removed` use the exact comparison semantics of the
844	  snapshot-id diff (JSON-object multisets, key order irrelevant, array order
845	  and value types significant, duplicates counted; entries
846	  `{"row", "count"}` sorted by canonical row text). `fields_added` and
847	  `fields_removed` compare the top-level field names appearing on the
848	  snapshots' row objects: names only on the target side are added, names only
849	  on the baseline side are removed, names on both enter neither set, and each
850	  list sorts by field name ascending. When both times select the same
851	  snapshot all four collections are empty and the request succeeds. Unknown
852	  dataset/version → `404`, checked before every request-shape check; a missing,
853	  blank, repeated, unparseable or timezone-less `from`/`to`, an extra query
854	  parameter or any request body bytes (whitespace-only included) → `422`; a
855	  side with no snapshot at or before its timestamp → `404` and nothing is
856	  written.
857	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at/masked-view` —
858	  role-masked time travel, appended one segment after the bare-row time
859	  lookup and accepting POST only. The body contains exactly `role` and
860	  `timestamp`: `{"role": "guest", "timestamp": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`; the
861	  service selects the latest snapshot whose `created_at` is not later than
862	  `timestamp` (the same selection as the bare-row lookup). On success it
863	  returns `{"dataset", "version", "snapshot_id", "created_at", "rows"}`; the
864	  `rows` are an order-preserving copy of the snapshot's rows masked exactly
865	  as the row-submission privacy view masks them, applying only the version's
866	  currently enabled policies (`redact`/`partial` semantics, `allowed_roles`,
867	  nulls and uncovered fields behave identically). Every successful read
868	  appends one masking-hit record per value actually masked, structurally
869	  identical to the regular view's hit records and continuing the same
870	  per-version sequence run, plus exactly one access record whose
871	  `row_count` is the snapshot's row count and whose `masked_count` equals
872	  the number of hit records written by the read. An empty snapshot, an
873	  allowed role, all-null values and a version without policies all succeed
874	  and leave only the access record. The records enter all existing
875	  masking-hit/access reads, filters, summaries, diffs, reconciliation,
876	  trends and cleanup previews; records of one read share a write timestamp,
877	  sequences stay continuous across processes, and a write obstruction never
878	  fails the read. The read never modifies or deletes the snapshot or its
879	  rows and never changes policies or identification records. Unknown
880	  dataset/version → `404`, and no snapshot existing at or before the
881	  timestamp is likewise `404`, both checked before every shape check (the
882	  latter whenever the body carries a usable timestamp); a missing or
883	  wrong-typed `role`/`timestamp`, a role blank after trimming, an
884	  unparseable or timezone-less timestamp, an extra body field, an empty,
885	  whitespace-only or non-JSON body, a non-object body and any query
886	  parameter are `422` and write nothing.
887	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/diff/{other_snapshot_id}` —
888	  compare two snapshots as JSON-object multisets. Object key order does not
889	  affect equality, while array order and JSON value types do (e.g. `1`, `1.0`,
890	  `"1"` and `true` are all distinct), and duplicate rows are counted. Both
891	  snapshots must belong to the dataset and version named in the path, otherwise
892	  `422`; unknown dataset/version/snapshot → `404`. The response is
893	  `{"from_snapshot_id", "to_snapshot_id", "added", "removed"}`; `added` lists
894	  rows present more often (or only) in the `to` snapshot and `removed` the
895	  converse, each entry being `{"row": {...}, "count": <int>}` sorted by the
896	  canonical (key-sorted) JSON text of `row`.
897	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/snapshots/{base_snapshot_id}/diff/{target_snapshot_id}` —
898	  read-only comparison of two snapshots belonging to two **different** schema
899	  versions of the path dataset; the baseline snapshot is named first and the
900	  target second, and either version order is allowed. It takes no request
901	  body and no query parameters (`422`). Unknown dataset or snapshot → `404`,
902	  checked ahead of every request-shape check; a snapshot owned by another
903	  dataset, or two snapshots of the same schema version (same-version
904	  comparisons still go through the snapshot-id diff endpoint) → `422`. The
905	  JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace,
906	  exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `base_snapshot_id`,
907	  `base_version`, `target_snapshot_id`, `target_version`, `field_changes`,
908	  `added` and `removed` in that order. `field_changes` lists only additions,
909	  removals, type changes and nullability changes of the two versions' field
910	  definitions, reusing the compatibility/trajectory literals (`added`,
911	  `removed`, `type_changed`, `nullable_tightened`, `nullable_loosened`);
912	  several changes of one field collapse into a single entry (a type change
913	  wins over a nullability change), entries sort by field name and each entry
914	  has `field`, `kind`, `before` and `after`, with the missing side `null`
915	  (never omitted). Rows are projected onto exactly the field names defined
916	  in both versions — other stored keys and fields absent from a row do not
917	  participate — and the projections are compared with the same-version
918	  snapshot diff's multiset semantics (object key order irrelevant, array
919	  order and value types significant, duplicates counted). `added` lists
920	  rows present more often or only on the target side, `removed` the
921	  converse, each entry `{"row", "count"}` sorted by the canonical
922	  (key-sorted) JSON text of the projected row. The comparison is fully
923	  read-only: snapshots, rows, field definitions, the lineage impact cache
924	  and every privacy trail are never touched, and the result is identical
925	  across process restarts.
926	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/quality-rules/evaluate`
927	  — evaluate the version's enabled quality rules over the snapshot's persisted
928	  rows. The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`);
929	  unknown dataset/version/snapshot → `404` (checked first), and a snapshot
930	  owned by another version → `422`. The response and the rule semantics are
931	  exactly those of the row-submission evaluation (`{"dataset", "version",
932	  "results"}`), the snapshot and its rows are never modified, and every
933	  successful evaluation appends the same immutable history summary (with
934	  `row_count` set to the snapshot's actual row count) that also feeds the
935	  evaluation diff and anomaly detection. An empty snapshot is recorded with
936	  zero violations.
937	
938	### Retention policies and lineage-aware snapshot deletion
939	
940	A schema version can carry a single retention policy; snapshot deletion is a
941	two-stage request/confirm flow that refuses to remove snapshots still feeding
942	downstream fields. Policies and requests are persisted across restarts.
943	
944	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/retention-policies` — create the
945	  version's one retention policy. Body: `{"retention_days": 30}` with a
946	  non-negative integer. Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`,
947	  `retention_days`, `created_at`. A second policy for the same version returns
948	  `409`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; other invalid input → `422`.
949	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/deletion-requests` —
950	  request deletion. Body contains only a non-empty `reason`. The snapshot and
951	  the version's retention policy must exist. Returns `201` with `id`,
952	  `snapshot_id`, `policy_id`, `reason`, `status`, `impacted`, `created_at`.
953	  `impacted` lists every field directly or indirectly reachable downstream of
954	  any field of the snapshot's version along lineage mappings; entries are
955	  deduplicated and sorted by dataset, version and field ascending. The request
956	  is `blocked` when any downstream field exists and `pending` otherwise. A
957	  second `pending`/`blocked` request for the same snapshot returns `409`.
958	- `GET .../snapshots/{snapshot_id}/deletion-requests` — list the snapshot's
959	  deletion requests sorted by `id` ascending. The collection remains
960	  addressable after a confirmed request has deleted its snapshot.
961	- `POST .../snapshots/{snapshot_id}/deletion-requests/{request_id}/confirm` —
962	  confirm a request (no body). Confirmation succeeds only while the request is
963	  `pending` and the snapshot is at least `retention_days` old; otherwise `409`
964	  and nothing is deleted. On success the snapshot is deleted atomically with
965	  the status change to `confirmed`, and the response adds `confirmed_at`. Once
966	  deleted, the snapshot no longer appears in snapshot read, list, `at` or diff
967	  responses.
968	
969	  Unknown dataset/version/snapshot/policy/request → `404`; other invalid input
970	  → `422` and nothing is written.
971	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/retention-sweep` —
972	  batch retention cleanup of the version's snapshots, appended one segment
973	  after the version's snapshot collection and accepting POST only. The body
974	  contains only a non-empty `reason`: `{"reason": "retention reached"}` (the
975	  trimmed reason is stored on every request the sweep opens). Every snapshot
976	  of the version is scanned in snapshot-id order: a snapshot whose age has
977	  reached the version's retention days (the same age judgment as the
978	  deletion-request confirmation) and that carries no open (`pending`/
979	  `blocked`) deletion request gets a new request with the submitted reason —
980	  `blocked` when the version feeds downstream fields and `pending` otherwise,
981	  the same status judgment as the single-snapshot entry. A snapshot with an
982	  open request is skipped (never duplicated, never modified) and a snapshot
983	  younger than the retention age is skipped and only counted; a version
984	  without snapshots sweeps successfully with empty collections. The whole
985	  scan runs in a single transaction — either every new request is written or
986	  none is — and concurrent sweeps of the same version have a single winner,
987	  the loser receiving `409` and changing nothing. The response is a
988	  deterministic JSON document (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly
989	  one trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`, `version`, `created`,
990	  `skipped` and `counts` in that order. `created` and `skipped` are sorted by
991	  snapshot id ascending; each entry has exactly `snapshot_id`, `request_id`,
992	  `status` and `reason` (skipped entries echo the existing open request).
993	  `counts` gives `created_count`, `skipped_count` and `not_due_count`, each
994	  equal to the number of snapshots in that category. The opened requests are
995	  ordinary deletion requests: they enter the existing deletion-request list
996	  and confirm flow, are deleted atomically on confirmation and persist across
997	  restarts. Unknown dataset/version → `404` (judged before every body/query
998	  shape check); a version without a registered retention policy → `404`; a
999	  missing, non-string or blank `reason`, an extra body field, an empty or
1000	  whitespace-only body, malformed JSON, a non-object body or any query
1001	  parameter → `422` and nothing is written.
1002	
1003	### Processing tasks
1004	
1005	A processing task is a named unit of work attached to a schema version; each
1006	run records one attempt. Tasks and runs are persisted across restarts.
1007	
1008	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks` — create a
1009	  task. Body: `{"name": "extract", "depends_on": [1], "max_attempts": 3}`.
1010	  `name` must be non-empty and unique within the version (`409` on conflict);
1011	  `depends_on` is an array of distinct task ids from the same version (default
1012	  `[]`, unknown ids → `404`); `max_attempts` is a positive integer (default
1013	  `1`). Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`, `name`, `depends_on`,
1014	  `max_attempts`, `status` (`pending`), `attempt_count` (`0`) and
1015	  `created_at`. Other invalid input → `422` and nothing is written.
1016	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks` — list tasks
1017	  sorted by `id` ascending.
1018	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}` —
1019	  return the task together with its `runs`, sorted by `attempt` ascending.
1020	  Each run has `id`, `task_id`, `attempt`, `status`, `started_at`,
1021	  `finished_at` and `error`. Unknown dataset/version/task → `404`.
1022	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs` —
1023	  start a new run. Only allowed while the task is `pending` or `failed`, has
1024	  attempts left (`attempt_count < max_attempts`) and every task in
1025	  `depends_on` has status `succeeded`; otherwise `409` and nothing is written.
1026	  Returns `201` with the new `running` run and increments the task's
1027	  `attempt_count` (the task becomes `running`).
1028	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/dispatch` —
1029	  worker batch claim. The body is optional and contains only an optional
1030	  `limit`: omit the body (or send `{}`) to claim one task, or send
1031	  `{"limit": <positive integer>}`. Within a single transaction, up to `limit`
1032	  startable tasks are selected by task id ascending; a task is startable when
1033	  it is `pending`, or `failed` with attempts left, and every direct dependency
1034	  is `succeeded` at selection time. Each selected task gets a new `running`
1035	  run for its next attempt, `attempt_count` is incremented and the task becomes
1036	  `running`. `running`, `succeeded`, attempt-exhausted and dependency-blocked
1037	  tasks are skipped; a task started earlier in the same request is only
1038	  `running`, so its dependents are not selectable until a later request.
1039	  Returns `201` with `{"dataset", "version", "runs"}`; `runs` is sorted by
1040	  task id ascending and each run has the same fields as the single-task start
1041	  endpoint. When no task is startable the response is still `201` with an
1042	  empty `runs` list. Concurrent dispatches (and dispatches interleaved with
1043	  single-task starts) never create a duplicate attempt or two running runs for
1044	  the same task, and a single response never exceeds `limit`. Unknown
1045	  dataset/version → `404`; extra body fields, a non-integer (including
1046	  boolean) or non-positive `limit` → `422` and nothing is written.
1047	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}` —
1048	  finish the currently running run. Body: `{"status": "succeeded"}` or
1049	  `{"status": "failed", "error": "<non-empty message>"}`. Writes `finished_at`
1050	  and moves the task to the same status; a `failed` task with attempts left
1051	  can be started again. Finishing an already finished run → `409`; a run that
1052	  does not belong to the task/version in the path → `422`; unknown
1053	  dataset/version/task/run → `404`; other invalid input → `422` and nothing
1054	  is written.
1055	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/batch-complete` —
1056	  finish several currently running runs in one transaction. Body contains only
1057	  a non-empty `runs` array; each item names a task of the path version and one
1058	  of its runs: `{"task_id": <int>, "run_id": <int>, "status": "succeeded"}` or
1059	  the same with `"status": "failed"` and an `error` that is non-empty after
1060	  trimming whitespace (`succeeded` items carry no `error`). The same task must
1061	  not appear twice. The whole batch is validated before any write and either
1062	  every item completes or none do; on success the response is
1063	  `{"dataset", "version", "runs"}` with the completed runs sorted by task id
1064	  ascending, each carrying the same fields as the single-run finish response.
1065	  Every run gets a `finished_at` timestamp and its task moves atomically to
1066	  the same status; `failed` tasks keep their consumed attempts and stay
1067	  retryable while attempts remain. Tasks whose dependencies succeed in the
1068	  same batch are not started or skipped within that batch (the dependencies
1069	  are `running` at selection time, as with dispatch) and become startable
1070	  immediately afterwards, each at its next continuous attempt. Empty/missing
1071	  `runs`, extra fields, non-integer (including boolean) ids, an unknown status
1072	  or a missing/blank/non-string `error` → `422`; an empty body or malformed
1073	  JSON → `422`; any query parameter → `422`. Unknown dataset/version → `404`;
1074	  a batch task that does not exist or belongs to another dataset/version →
1075	  `404`; an unknown run → `404` (a run belonging to another dataset/version is
1076	  treated as out of scope); a run that belongs to another task of the same
1077	  version → `422`. An already finished run, a duplicate task in the batch or a
1078	  task that is not currently `running` (not currently completable) → `409`,
1079	  and the entire batch is rolled back: statuses, timestamps and counters are
1080	  unchanged. Concurrent batch completion is single-winner against the
1081	  single-run finish/cancel endpoints, run starts and batch dispatch: exactly
1082	  one racing operation commits and the others receive `409`, never leaving a
1083	  `running` run with a half-written `finished_at` or rolling `attempt_count`
1084	  back. Audit records appended afterwards record the run's terminal status,
1085	  and the schedule, audit report and post-restart reads present the batch
1086	  results through the existing fields and ordering.
1087	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}/cancel` —
1088	  cancel the currently running run. The body contains only a non-empty
1089	  `reason` string; leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed and the result
1090	  is stored as the run's `error`. Returns the updated run with `finished_at`
1091	  written and `status` `failed`; the task is atomically moved to `failed` in
1092	  the same transaction while `attempt_count` is not rolled back, so a
1093	  cancelled task follows the existing start rules: it can run again when its
1094	  dependencies have succeeded and attempts remain, and the next run keeps the
1095	  continuous attempt sequence. Only a `running` run can be cancelled;
1096	  cancelling an already `succeeded`/`failed` run returns `409` and changes no
1097	  field. A run that does not belong to the task/version in the path → `422`;
1098	  unknown dataset/version/task/run → `404`; a missing reason, an extra body
1099	  field, a non-string reason or one that is blank after trimming, an empty
1100	  body, malformed JSON or any query parameter → `422` and nothing is
1101	  written. Cancellation is single-winner against finishing, single-task
1102	  starts and batch dispatch: exactly one racing operation performs the state
1103	  transition and the others receive `409`, so no run is left `running` with a
1104	  half-written `finished_at`.
1105	- `PUT /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/dependencies` —
1106	  atomically replace the task's dependency list. Body contains only
1107	  `{"depends_on": [<task id>, ...]}` (the array may be empty); the ids must
1108	  reference existing tasks of the same version without duplicates and must not
1109	  include the target task itself. The replacement is rejected when the target
1110	  task is not `pending` or when it would introduce a cycle in the dependency
1111	  graph; on success the updated task is returned. Unknown
1112	  dataset/version/task/dependency → `404`; a self dependency, a cycle or a
1113	  non-`pending` target → `409`; any other invalid body → `422` and nothing is
1114	  written. The existing run-start rule uses the updated dependencies.
1115	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/schedule` —
1116	  return `{"dataset", "version", "tasks"}` with tasks sorted by `id` ascending.
1117	  Each task carries every processing-task field plus `schedule_state` and
1118	  `blocking_task_ids`. `schedule_state` is `running` or `succeeded` for tasks
1119	  in those states; a `failed` task is `retryable` while attempts remain and
1120	  `exhausted` once they are used up; a `pending` task is `ready` when all of
1121	  its direct dependencies have succeeded, `upstream_failed` when any
1122	  dependency chain contains an `exhausted` or `upstream_failed` task, and
1123	  `blocked` otherwise. `blocking_task_ids` lists the direct dependencies that
1124	  have not succeeded, sorted ascending; it is empty for non-pending tasks.
1125	  States are recomputed on every read (including after a successful retry)
1126	  and both the dependency graph and the schedule survive restarts.
1127	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/audit-report` —
1128	  read-only audit report for the whole version; the endpoint takes no request
1129	  body and no query parameters (both are rejected with `422`; unknown
1130	  dataset/version → `404`). Returns
1131	  `{"dataset", "version", "summary", "tasks"}`. `summary` contains
1132	  `task_count`, `run_count`, `pending_tasks`, `running_tasks`,
1133	  `succeeded_tasks`, `failed_tasks`, `exhausted_tasks` and
1134	  `invalid_audit_runs`; status counters count tasks by their stored status,
1135	  `exhausted_tasks` counts `failed` tasks that have used up
1136	  `max_attempts`, and `invalid_audit_runs` counts runs whose audit chain fails
1137	  re-verification. `tasks` is sorted by task `id` and each task carries every
1138	  processing-task field plus `runs`; `runs` is sorted by `attempt` and each
1139	  run carries its run fields plus `proof`. `proof` re-runs the same checks as
1140	  the per-run verify endpoint over that run's audit chain and is
1141	  `{"valid", "checked_count", "last_evidence_hash"}`; `last_evidence_hash` is
1142	  the stored evidence hash of the chain's final record and is `null` only for
1143	  an empty chain — it is still returned when `valid` is `false`, and the run
1144	  details are retained. Summary counters always agree with the returned
1145	  details and the report is deterministic across restarts.
1146	
1147	### Processing run audit records (append-only proof chain)
1148	
1149	Every run carries an independent, tamper-evident chain of audit records.
1150	Records are append-only (the database rejects updates and deletes, and there
1151	are no per-record HTTP routes), numbered from `1` per run and linked through
1152	SHA-256 evidence hashes. They persist across restarts.
1153	
1154	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}/audit-records` —
1155	  append a record. Body contains exactly `event`, `input_summary` and
1156	  `result_summary`, each a string that is non-empty after trimming whitespace.
1157	  Returns `201` with the submitted fields plus `id`, `sequence` (continuous
1158	  from `1` within the run), `run_status` (the run's status at write time:
1159	  `running`/`succeeded`/`failed`), `previous_hash` (`null` for the first
1160	  record, otherwise the previous record's `evidence_hash`), `evidence_hash`
1161	  and `created_at`. Missing, extra, non-string or blank fields → `422` and
1162	  nothing is written; unknown dataset/version/task/run → `404`; a run that
1163	  does not belong to the path task (including one in another version) →
1164	  `422`. Concurrent appends never reuse a sequence or break the chain.
1165	- `GET .../runs/{run_id}/audit-records` — list the run's records in ascending
1166	  `sequence` order. Same `404`/`422` path rules.
1167	- `GET .../runs/{run_id}/audit-records/verify` — verify the chain. Returns the
1168	  path identifiers together with `valid` and `checked_count`:
1169	  `{"dataset", "version", "task_id", "run_id", "valid", "checked_count"}`.
1170	  Verification recomputes every `evidence_hash`, checks that `sequence` values
1171	  are continuous from `1` and that each `previous_hash` equals the preceding
1172	  record's `evidence_hash` (the first must be `null`). An intact chain returns
1173	  `"valid": true` (also for an empty chain).
1174	
1175	`evidence_hash` is the hexadecimal SHA-256 of a canonical JSON document built
1176	from every stored field except `id`, `created_at` and `evidence_hash` itself
1177	(`event`, `input_summary`, `result_summary`, `sequence`, `run_status`,
1178	`previous_hash`): keys are sorted by Unicode code point, no insignificant
1179	whitespace is emitted and the text is UTF-8 encoded.
1180
